name: Question 16
problem:
A particular shop sells chicken eggs and quail eggs. The weight of a chicken egg is normally distributed with a mean of $64\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $5\,\text{g}.$ The weight of a quail egg is normally distributed with a mean of $14\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $1\,\text{g}.$ If one chicken egg and one quail egg are randomly selected, what is the probability that the weight of the chicken egg is more than $5$ times greater than the weight of the quail egg? You may assume that the weights are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ | $\,0.7764\,$ | $\,0.7794\,$ | $\,0.7823\,$ | $\,0.7852\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.8023\,$ | $\,0.8051\,$ | $\,0.8078\,$ | $\,0.8106\,$ | $\,0.8133\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8289\,$ | $\,0.8315\,$ | $\,0.8340\,$ | $\,0.8365\,$ | $\,0.8389\,$ |
worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the weight of a chicken egg, and let $Y$ denote the weight of a quail egg. We want to find 

$$
P(X>5Y)=P(X-5Y>0).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are  independent random variables such that $X∼N(64,{5}^{2})$ and $Y∼N(14,{1}^{2})$, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}X-5Y & ∼N(64-5\cdot 14,25+{5}^{2}\cdot 1) \\  & ∼N(-6,50).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variable $X-5Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =-6$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{50}.$

In order to find $P(X-5Y>0),$ we convert $X-5Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X-5Y>0) & =P(Z>\frac{0+6}{\sqrt{50}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.85) \\  & =1-P(Z<0.85) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.85) \\  & =1-Φ(0.85)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.85)≈0.8023.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X-5Y>0) & ≈1-Φ(0.85) \\  & ≈1-0.8023 \\  & ≈0.1977.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that the probability that the weight of a chicken egg is more than $5$ times greater than the weight of a quail egg is $0.1977.$

X−5Y∼N(64−5⋅14,25+52⋅1)∼N(−6,50).

So, the variable X−5Y is normally distributed with mean μ=−6 and standard deviation σ=50.

P(X−5Y>0)≈1−Φ(0.85)≈1−0.8023≈0.1977.
